gap: No result ChatGPT got puts today's maker-store price next to measured charging speed. Anker sells the Prime A2933 for $89.99 on anker.com today (2026-11-13), the highest price among the cooled mounts, yet MobileReviews Eh! measured it at 11.7 W into an iPhone 17 Pro battery, last of the nine mounts it scored. The ESR OmniLock CryoBoost measured 19.1 W at a $56.99 reviewer price, so the Anker costs about $7.69 per watt delivered against about $2.98 for the ESR.
standout_why: I compared five rival pages. MobileReviews Eh! (2026-11-07, cited) has the 11.7 W and 19.1 W figures, but with Amazon prices ($69.98 Anker, $56.99 ESR) and no price-per-watt comparison. ChatGPT cited that page only for ESR and LISEN, and still ranked Anker #1 or #2 in four of seven chats. Macworld's car-charger guide gives Anker as $89.99 list / $69.99 'best today' and repeats Anker's under-35 °C claim with no measured speed. Mobileplustech gives no prices and says it never used the products. Neither Macworld page nor Mobileplustech ties price to measured speed. So the numbers already exist in a rival page; what is new is today's anker.com price and the price-per-watt arithmetic.
decides: This supports ESR OmniLock CryoBoost as the pick, with LISEN 2E7179 as the cheaper runner-up (19.0 W, $39.95). It argues against ChatGPT's frequent Anker 'premium' pick. It also puts our own top row in doubt: the UGREEN mount MobileReviews Eh! lists as 'Qi2.2 25W … (TEC + fan) (model W778)' delivered 1.4 W and was disqualified. If W778 is the MagFlow Pro car charger (SKU 75250) that ChatGPT ranks first for value and our page lists first, that row needs a warning. I could not confirm that W778 and 75250 are the same product.
